en: ENTIA (Epistemic Notation for Texts In Archives) is an editorial notation for curated archives. Here an archive means a curated collection of published texts, kept and maintained by whoever curates it — the corpus of a site, not an archival fonds and not unpublished records. For each item the notation declares what that item is for whoever keeps the collection: not what the item is about, but what function it performs in the collection that holds it. The notation has two axes. Five layers, ordered by decreasing arbitrariness, each defined by what it cannot do: free tag, topic, theme, concept, geometry. A free tag asserts nothing and generates no page; a concept asserts a proposition about the world and is rejected by an automated check if it arrives without a note or without declared relations. Six reading functions, of which exactly one is assigned to each item, by hand, following a fixed precedence; the automated check verifies that the assignment is well formed, it does not produce it. ENTIA is an open protocol: the structure is fixed, while the vocabulary and the weighting parameters are replaced locally. Conformance requires publishing the assignments with their dates, publishing the distribution profile, declaring known disagreements between the rule and the judgement, and versioning the derived copy. The specification, the SKOS vocabulary and the corpus it was derived from are deposited under CC BY 4.0.

extent: 476 terms (2026-11): 6 functions, 5 themes, 59 topics, 406 concepts. Functions and themes are fixed by the specification; topics and concepts are local to the archive and grow with it — current counts in https://claudiocammarano.com/entia.json
